articles.title: The Open: Rory McIlroy right to criticise Bryson DeChambeau 'circus' - should players have to speak with the media?
articles.summary: Dame Laura Davies reflects on Rory McIlroy's comments about Bryson DeChambeau during The Open, the controversial two-shot penalty at Royal Birkdale and McIlroy's performance in the final men's major of the year
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy has always been the one that has been sticking up for the PGA Tour and I think he just gets fed up with the likes of DeChambeau. I just think he's had enough of the circus and I don't blame him.

I don't think it was the rules infringement itself that annoyed McIlroy, his main focus I thought was the fact that DeChambeau said 'I'm not going to play' and it delayed the draw.

McIlroy was very clever in his wording. He said a few of the guys were up in the player lounge and saw it in real time, so they weren't surprised that there was a problem in the scorer's tent.

The speculation on Friday evening that DeChambeau was not going to play over the weekend was pathetic. That's putting yourself above the game and saying you think you're more important than the game and The Open. He's not and if we can still play without Tiger Woods, I think the game's doing alright.

In my mind, speaking to the media was part of the job. In my day, when I was decent, every single round you were asked questions after the round and you answered them - that's what you're supposed to do.

Sometimes it's very difficult when you've just shot five over, blown a tournament, and media want to speak to you. I think that's more understandable, but he was doing really well at Royal Birkdale and still refusing.

I know he's missed a cut in the majors and that's where we're seeing him more, but he's made this point of not talking to the media. It needs to be 'keep this up and you will not be invited back' - that would be my line, because I think it's unacceptable.

As professional sports people, this is part of the job. The media is part of the job and you either embrace it and get on with it, or you cause problems the way he's causing problems.

Clumsy would be my assessment of McIlroy's week. The good shots have been amazing, and the ninth hole has been ridiculous, but every time he makes a step forward, he has made a step backwards.

I'm not sure I ever fancied McIlroy this week anyway, just because the course was so hard and fast and I really don't think that suits him. He has given it everything, like he always does, but hit too many poor shots and his putting has not been good enough.

I don't think he putts particularly well on what would be perceived as slow greens and, on these greens, he has not holed enough putts. His chipping hasn't been as sharp but I'd say ball-striking-wise it's been okay.

If you've won one of four majors you've had a brilliant season in the majors, so I think he'd be happy with one, although he would have loved two! There's so many good players now that you can't be disappointed with just one major.

He's got very high standards though and he potentially would have expected a couple. Our expectations of him and what he can actually produce is a little bit skewed really, but he makes it look easy sometimes.

articles.title: AIG Women's Open: How major continues 'unrecognisable' rise ahead of 50th anniversary at Royal Lytham & St Annes
articles.summary: Ahead of the 50th anniversary of the inaugural AIG Women's Open, Dame Laura Davies reflects on the how the tournament has evolved to record-breaking prize purses and one of the biggest events on the golfing calendar; watch all four rounds exclusively live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Step forward a half-century and the tournament is unrecognizable to the one Jenny Lee Smith won at Fulford Golf Club in 1976, having evolved into one of the biggest events in the golfing calendar.

Whereas the inaugural edition saw professionals Vivien Saunders and Gwen Brandom among those contributing their own money towards the prize fund, the tournament has since gone from strength to strength with enhanced infrastructure and purse increases.

A star-studded field returns to Royal Lytham & St Annes for the 50th anniversary this week, live from Thursday on Sky Sports , where the world's best will challenge for major glory and a record $1.5m (£1.25m) winner's share of a $10m (£7.5m) prize purse.

"I don't recognise it from when I used to play it," Dame Laura Davies, who made a record 43 consecutive AIG Women's Open appearances, told Sky Sports . "It's not an add-on anymore, it's a stand-alone major championship of golf and it's a superb event."

Over 50,000 fans are expected at Royal Lytham & St Annes across tournament week, having broken different attendance records each of the previous three editions, while AIG have more than trebled the prize money on offer since becoming title sponsors.

A rocky start to the tournament's history saw it not have a sponsor until 1979 and initially struggle to attract venues to host the event, while the 1983 edition was cancelled due to a lack of funding and left its future under threat.

The LPGA Tour had it as part of their 1984 schedule but wouldn't again for another decade, with Burberry (1985) and Weetabix (1987-1993) among the sponsors during that stint, with the tournament taking time to grow in stature.

"My very first Open was in 1980 at Wentworth on the East Course, then we went up to Newcastle (1981) and there was nobody there," Davies added. "Then we went to Woburn for a long time and the galleries were really good.

"I won my Women's Open at Royal Birkdale (1986) and I think there was a couple of hundred people walking around on the final round, so you just can't compare to how it is now - it has grown massively."

The tournament was first recognised as a major in 2001, replacing the event now known as the Canadian Women's Open, while it only started directly being organised by the R&A - rather than the Ladies' Golf Union - in 2017.

The Old Course at St Andrews, Carnoustie and Royal Troon are all on The Open roster and have been recent venues for the AIG Women's Open, while extended TV coverage and award-winning player facilities have helped the tournament thrive.

"I think the biggest thing is that we go to all these great links courses," Davies explained. "Obviously prize money is a big thing and goes up and up every year, which the players certainly love, but it's also the facilities.

"When you get there and see the infrastructure, the player lounge and the services for the players, it just makes you feel comfortable and makes you feel special. Everyone's looked after as a player and they do a great job.

"Obviously women's sport being more on TV now helps, because people want to come and see the characters they see on TV, and you've seen that gallery-wise and how much they've grown. I can't say anything bad about this event!"

Huge week ahead at Royal Lytham…and another British winner?

Featured Group coverage will provide three hours of extra action over the first two rounds of the final women's major of the year, where Nelly Korda looks to complete the career Grand Slam and Haeran Ryu chases a third consecutive major title.

The last two winners of the AIG Women's Open at Royal Lytham have both been British, with Georgia Hall's 2018 success following Catriona Matthew's 2009 win, while Charley Hull and Lottie Woad are among those looking to extend that streak on home soil.

"I spoke to a couple of the caddies that were at Royal Birkdale [for The Open] and have been there [Royal Lytham] - they've said it's really fiery," Davies said. "Bunkers are going to be a nightmare, because they're a lot harsher than the ones at Royal Birkdale.

"Hull never really got in contention at the Evian Championship and we'll have to wait and see whether her course management works here. She's going to win a major - she's too good not to.

"From what I hear from all the other caddies about Lottie [Woad], she's very solid. She's not flashy, has a really good temperament and takes it all in her stride. If you can have that temperament, then it's a huge thing."

Who will win the AIG Women's Open? Watch throughout the week live on Sky Sports. Live coverage of the opening round begins on Thursday with Featured Groups from 9am, ahead of full coverage from 1pm on Sky Sports Golf.

articles.title: Amgen Irish Open: Shane Lowry retains lead of home event as Donald Trump arrives despite protests
articles.summary: Shane Lowry leads by four shots heading into the weekend, clear of Denmark's Jacob Skov Olesen who carded a bogey at the last; play was delayed just before 3pm as Donald Trump's helicopter landed to allow him to watch Rory McIlroy on the 18th green
articles.body:
The home favourite delighted fans at Trump International Links in Doonbeg, on a day when the US President paid a visit to the course bearing his name.

After breaking the course record on Friday , Lowry carried on his superb form into the weekend with only Dane Jacob Skov Olesen remaining close, as he looked set to match the leader's 65 on Saturday.

But after Lowry holed out for par on 18, Olesen was unable to make his putt so carded a disappointing bogey at the last, following an excellent round.

Lowry retains the clubhouse lead at 16-under par for the tournament with Olesen four shots adrift. The next closest player is Joaquin Niemann, who led after Thursday, at nine under.

"Anytime you play a links golf in 15-20mph winds and it got a little cold at the end there, it's going to be hard and you're going to have some testers for pars," Lowry said.

"I felt like I did a great job today of just staying in the moment and playing my own game. Yeah, I had, you know, so much fun out there on the back nine.

"The crowds were incredible. They cheered me on the whole way home and hopefully will do the same tomorrow."

Donald Trump landed just in time to see Rory McIlroy hole out on 18, but the Northern Irishman had a day to forget. His 76 leaves him well out of contention heading into Sunday.

"I guess not the experience we're used to in a way," said McIlroy. "I think it's Air Force One's maiden voyage, I think, so that was pretty cool.

"Cool to sort of see all that going on. I was trying to avoid making doubles at that point so I was trying to concentrate on my own stuff as well."

Trump ignores protests across country to attend Irish Open

Thousands protested against Donald Trump's two-day visit to Ireland on Sunday, with organisers claiming a turnout in the tens of thousands in Dublin.

Sinn Féin and the Greens were among the political parties taking part, and the Irish Gardaí police force mounted a major security operation as the protest disrupted traffic and public transport in the city centre.

Smaller demonstrations were held at Shannon Airport, where the US military's use of the airport for transit and refuelling is a long-standing grievance, and in the village of Doonbeg, close to the course.

Trump had completed a series of engagements in Dublin and left the city before the main march began.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Team Europe regain trophy from Team USA after Lottie Woad, Carlota Ciganda close out thrilling home win
articles.summary: Lottie Woad took Team Europe to 14 points before Carlota Ciganda confirmed a home victory over Team USA at Bernardus Golf; Anna Nordqvist's side regained the trophy with a 15-13 win on a rainy final day in the Netherlands
articles.body:
Europe went into a rainy Sunday at Bernardus Golf tied 8-8 and requiring at least 6.5 points for victory, two years on from losing to Team USA, with Charley Hull leading from the front to beat Megan Khang 3&2 and put early blue on the board.

Anna Nordqvist's side briefly led in eight of the 12 matches and moved further ahead when Linn Grant beat Angel Yin, completing her perfect week, but Alison Lee gave Team USA hope with a record comeback from four down to beat Esther Henseleit 1up.

World No 1 Nelly Korda levelled the contest when she saw off rookie Mimi Rhodes 4&3, but wins for Nastasia Nadaud, Nanna Koerstz Madsen and Julia Lopez Ramirez moved Europe closer to victory.

Lottie Woad beat Auston Kim to take the hosts to 14 points and sparked European celebrations, with Ciganda guaranteed at least a half-point, before the veteran - whose singles win 2023 saw them retain in Spain - defeated Jennifer Kupcho to confirm home victory.

How Team Europe claimed Europe on Solheim Cup glory

Kupcho's sensational late birdies on Saturday evening had left Team USA captain Angela Stanford feeling like they had 'turned the tide' in their favour, only for Team Europe to quickly take charge on the final day.

Hull thrashed Korda 6&4 in the singles two years and was trusted to lead out Europe again, despite registering 0.5 points with Woad over the first four sessions, with the Englishwoman validating Nordqvist's decision by claiming a full point.

The eight-time Solheim Cup player won the opening hole with the par and never trailed against Khang, with Hull matching the American's birdie at the eighth and then winning both par-fives on the back nine to close out victory.

"I've been giving myself so many chances, so that's been quite frustrating," Hull admitted. "Obviously didn't hole a lot today, but I was just very steady, hit a lot of greens."

Grant became just the ninth player in history to post a 4-0-0 record or after a dominant 4&3 win over Yin, with American Lee matching the Swede's record by coming back from four down with seven holes to stun Henseleit in match two.

" I just did my best to stay consistent," Lee said. "That front nine was pretty tough with the rain coming down. I couldn't give myself birdie chances and put myself in a good spot. Thankfully the weather turned around, and my golf game did as well."

Korda produced her performance of the week against Rhodes but Europe's other three rookies all returned points, with Nadaud seeing off Andrea Lee 3&2 for a third win of her debut before Lopez Ramirez capped off an unbeaten debut by beating Yealimi Noh.

Madsen had seen off Allisen Corpuz before Woad recovered from losing three consecutive holes on the back nine to beat Kim and leave Europe on the brink, after a brief period of Team USA momentum, while Ciganda quickly built an early lead against Kupcho and claimed the winning point.

"I'm so happy," Ciganda said. "I think we had a great team all week. I think it's been one of the best teams that we've had in the last few years."

Team USA rookie Lindy Duncan ended Maja Stark's perfect record and Lauren Coughlin inflicted Leona Maguire's first ever Solheim singles defeat, reducing the winning margin, while Rose Zhang beat Celine Boutier 2up in the bottom match to leave the Frenchwoman without a point for her week.

Nordqvist savours 'amazing' win as Stanford praises Europe

"There's just been so much hard work this week and in the last two years leading up to this from not only me, but all the background team. The helpers have been amazing this week, making it easy for the players just to play.

"We just had a really good vibe all week. Everyone's been really good team-mates. We talked a lot about the fast starts this week with the way the golf course was. I'm just really, really proud of the players for starting strong and even finishing strong."

"I think that we did a lot of things right leading up to it and I know we did. They fought hard and we seemed to always be on the same page.

"The Europeans played great today and that's the way it goes. Their backs were against the wall, they had nothing to lose, and that's exactly what they did. They came out and played well, so good for them."

Back to winning ways: Europe's win in numbers

That was Europe's eighth win in 20 editions of the Solheim Cup and their first since 2021, while Europe have now won six of the 10 Solheim Cups on home soil.

Seven points won in the singles is Europe's best return since the 7.5 they earned in 2013.

Linn Grant top-scored for Team Europe with four points from four matches, despite winning zero points from four in 2024.

Carlota Ciganda becomes the second European in history to win multiple Solheim Cup-clinching points, joining Catriona Matthew (2003 and 2013)

Nastasia Nadaud and Mimi Rhodes became the first rookie pair in history to win two matches together

The Ladies European Tour heads to Spain next for La Sella Open, beginning Thursday and held at La Sella Golf Resort, while the LPGA Tour takes a week off before the Walmart N Arkansas Championship from September 25-27.

articles.title: Amgen Irish Open: Shane Lowry secures record 11-stroke victory at Trump International Links in Doonbeg
articles.summary: Shane Lowry cards eight birdies in final-round 63, including one at the 18th to sign off his stunning triumph in style; Rory McIlory defiant, saying "I don't feel too far away" after signing off disappointing title defence with a round of 67 to finish one under
articles.body:
It's Lowry's seventh career title and his second Irish Open triumph, following his 2009 victory as a 22-year-old amateur, with US President Donald Trump presenting him with the trophy.

It's a welcome return to the winner's circle for Lowry after a series of agonising near-misses earlier this season, including a double-bogey on the final hole that cost him the Dubai Invitational by two strokes and a collapse at the Cognizant Classic, where he surrendered a three-stroke lead with three holes to play by closing with two double-bogeys.

The result was never in doubt at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, however, as Lowry - holding a four-shot lead heading into Sunday - extended his advantage with a superb final round, while Trump watched on for the second consecutive day.

Crowds cheered Donald Trump and chanted "USA" as he told them he was removing tariffs from Irish whiskey, saying he had discussed the matter with Taoiseach Micheal Martin, minister for sport, who was also on the 18th green for the prizegiving ceremony, along with Charlie McConalogue, minister for state.

Lowry hails 'spectacular week' | 'I can't wait to bring trophy home'

Lowry carded eight birdies for his round and just one bogey, at the ninth, with a pair of stunning 45-foot putts at the par-three seventh and par-four 15th sending the watching crowd into a frenzy. He capped his victory in style with another long-range birdie at the last.

"This year has been quite difficult on the course for me," an emotional Lowry said after his triumph. "I've had a few chances to win, and there's been some really tough times.

"To come here this week and do this, I don't do things by half measures! I can't believe I'm standing here with that leaderboard.

"This has been the most spectacular week. It has been unreal.

"When things are not going well at this level, it's hard at home as well, but my wife's been a huge support, and my kids. I just love them so much and I'm so happy for them. I can't wait to bring a trophy home.

"My daughter is always ask me when you're going to bring a trophy home. So, yes, I'm going to bring one home."

Lowry had taken such a sizeable advantage into Sunday in large part thanks to breaking the course record with a second-round 62 on Friday

Jacob Skov Olesen, Lowry's closest challenger at 12 under and four shots back overnight, slipped down the leaderboard with a three-over 73. Patrick Reed's closing 64 and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen's 63 were impressive enough to earn them second and third respectively, but Lowry had already surged clear.

Joaquin Niemann took a share of second with Reed on 12 under, with Neergaard-Petersen one back.

England's Alex Fitzpatrick was tied-seventh at nine under, a closing 64 from Sergio Garcia had him six under, on the same score as Robert MacIntyre and Matt Wallace, among others.

Jon Rahm finished four under and reigning champion Rory McIlroy rounded off a disappointing week with his best round of 67 to end his title defence one under.

McIlroy positive despite disappointing defence: 'I don't feel too far away'

McIlroy said his final round has given him some encouragement to take into next week at the BMW Championship at Wentworth, a tournament he won in 2014 and has been runner-up at three times since.

"I've seen enough good stuff this week to give me encouragement going into next week," McIlroy said. "It's a golf course that I know well and one I've had success on.

"Obviously this wasn't the week that I wanted but, at the same time, I don't feel too far away and I feel good going into Wentworth.

"I thought I hit the ball pretty well for the most part. A couple of bad decisions off the tees yesterday but, overall, my iron play was a lot better, my wedge play was pretty good for the most part and obviously it was a struggle on the greens.

"That was the difficult thing and why I wasn't able to get myself into contention. I need a little bit of time on the putting green the next couple days and to get familiar with the greens at Wentworth again."

The DP World Tour heads to Wentworth in Surrey next for the BMW PGA Championship.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: How Team Europe celebrated win over Team USA and Anna Nordqvist's side delivered home victory
articles.summary: Talking points from Team Europe's Solheim Cup victory over Team USA at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, including big celebrations after Anna Nordqvist's side impressed on a final day and Charley Hull, Lottie Woad, Carlota Ciganda, Linn Grant all delivered
articles.body:
That was the chant echoing around the Team Europe bus on Sunday evening after another Solheim Cup home success, where Anna Nordqvist overcame Team USA on the final day to regain the trophy.

The contest had been delicately poised heading into a rainy sit singles session at Bernardus Golf, with the momentum seemingly with the Americans after late drama in the Saturday fourballs saw them pull the match back into an 8-8 tie.

Jennifer Kupcho had holed over 110 feet of putts over her final two holes to snatch victory with Lindy Duncan over Carlota Ciganda and Celine Boutier, a result Team USA captain Angela Stanford said had "turned the tide" in their favour.

A video of the American team drinking beers on their bus that evening ended up being a premature celebration and an easy motivator for Team Europe, who won six of the top eight singles matches to regain control of the contest.

Lottie Woad's point-winning moment will be remembered as the one that clinched the Solheim Cup, taking Europe to 14 points with Carlota Ciganda already guaranteed at least a half-point, but it was the Spaniard who closed out her win and made it official.

Boisterous scenes around the course and in the trophy presentation continued off it, with a viral social media clip of Dame Laura Davies handing out beers to the European team on the bus and their celebrations running long into the night.

A final score of 15-13 didn't really reflect the final-day dominance of Nordqvist's side, with Team USA's largely flat top order - Nelly Korda and Alison Lee aside - unable to follow up their jubilance of the previous night and put pressure on Europe.

Few embrace the Solheim Cup more than Ciganda, who went from Europe's first-tee supporter in the opening session to producing multiple clutch moments as the week progressed.

The veteran was Europe's hero on Friday, where a dramatic final-hole par gave her and Julia Lopez Ramirez a half-point that avoided Team USA leading after day one, then was on the receiving end of Kupcho's birdie-birdie finish the following day.

Ciganda gained revenged over Kupcho in the singles and closed out her eighth appearance in style, becoming just the second player in history to earn the clinching point in two different Solheim Cups.

" I was really happy to see that I was playing against Kupcho," Ciganda admitted. "She's a fighter, I'm a fighter. I knew she had no chance. I was like, 'I want to kill you', so I had it very clear in my mind."

Charley Hull and Woad became the first pairing ever to tandem in all four sessions and broke several unwanted records during a disappointing first two days, despite playing better than their scores suggested.

They were both inside the top four for European birdies made over those sessions but returned just 0.5 points, with a record-equalling 6&5 loss in the Saturday morning foursomes among the three defeats.

Nordqvist was questioned for not splitting the pair on day two and came under further scrutiny for sending out Hull in the singles, a decision she described as a "no-brainer" before watching the 30-year-old earn Europe's first point of the day.

Hull said it was a "frustrating" week that saw her and Woad struggle to hole putts, with both - until their singles victories - in danger of becoming the first to participate in five sessions and not have any wins.

"Being the leader of this team, we knew she [Hull] was going to deliver," Nordqvist said. "It was blue on the board early. Lottie [Woad] has been very steady this week - it was nice to see her finally hole some putts"

Grant joins exclusive club as Europe's MVP

Team Europe's star performance came from Linn Grant, who became the first player to go from earning zero points in the previous Solheim Cup to earn at least four points in the next.

Grant became only the ninth player to go 4-0 or better during a Solheim Cup, with three victories alongside Maja Stark followed by a commanding 4&3 win over Angel Yin in the singles.

The all-Swedish pairing between the close friends was also seen in the 2023 edition and likely again in future Solheim Cups, with Grant overcoming shocking pre-event form - having five missed cuts in six starts - to finish as Europe's leading scorer.

"That is a really cool feeling that you have a person like this on your team, that you know you can just go out and you know them inside and out and their game," Stark explained about Grant. "It felt like, for Anna, it was a no-brainer to put us together."

Europe's captain's picks all delivered at least 1.5 points each, with Leona Maguire stepping up - in another record-breaking display - and the other three rookies contributing to push Nordqvist's side to the target required.

Maguire won both foursomes sessions alongside Esther Henseleit to become the quickest player to reach 10 match wins, taking just 14 matches and one faster than the previous record.

She briefly had the highest winning percentage in Solheim Cup history until her loss alongside Celine Boutier in the fourballs, while Ramirez responded to being left out throughout Saturday to finish unbeaten from her two matches.

"I said from the beginning her picks were really good," Stanford insisted, having seen her three picks deliver five points for Team USA. "She picked well because this golf course needed high-ball hitters and that's what she did."

Rhodes shines in 'unexpected' partnership

Had the final round of the AIG Women's Open played out differently last month, Rhodes would likely not have teed it up in the Netherlands. Instead, she leaves this week as a strong Team Europe options for many Solheim Cups ahead.

Henseleit finishing runner-up at Royal Lytham - the final qualifying event - saw her overtake Chiara Tamburlini in the European points list, securing Nanna Koerstz Madsen qualification via the world rankings and freeing up an extra captain's pick.

Rhodes took full advantage and was an instant hit, revelling in the first-tee spotlight and forming a winning partnership in both foursomes and foursomes with Nastasia Nadaud - the first rookie pairing to win two matches together at a Solheim Cup.

"A lot of people questioned why would you send out two rookies, but I said why not?!" Nordqvist explained. "And they delivered. I never felt like they were rookies."

Only Grant ended the week with more points for Team Europe than Nadaud, who was barely inside the world's top 150 a year ago but continued her meteoric rise with a Solheim Cup debut to remember.

A strong friendship off the course with Rhodes fuelled an equally impressive dynamic on it, with their 4&3 foursomes win on Saturday morning matching the largest-winning margin by a rookie pair.

Her performance that morning - where she was surprised to have even been selected - led to her being sent back out with Maguire that day, while her 3&2 singles win over Andrea Lee came at a time where Team USA threatened to wrestle back some control.

"Getting three points for Europe is just absolutely crazy - got no words for that," said Nadaud, who will now have her sights set on representing Europe again in years to come. "Everything just happened so fast!"

It would be little surprise to see the majority of Nordqvist's winning dozen back together in the future to try and win on away soil, given seven of them will still be aged under 30 for the 2028 edition in Virginia.

Four rookies making an immediate impact only highlighted the strength and depth of Europe's options, given the home victory came without recent Solheim Cup regulars Georgia Hall, Emily Kristine Pedersen and Madelene Sagstrom.

It was also the first Solheim Cup since 2007 without Nordqvist being involved as a player, having announced her retirement mid-season and ruling herself out of a captain's pick, but could the Swede be back again in the future?

"You're never going to say never," Nordqvist said in their victory press conference, when asked if she would consider taking on captaincy again in 2028. "I don't know what my future holds."

When Europe last won outright on home soil in 2019, Catriona Matthew returned as captain again to lead them to away glory in the following edition. Whether it's Nordqvist at the wheel or not in Virginia, that will be the next target.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy plays down concerns for DP World Tour players over PGA Tour qualifying criteria
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy returns to play at the BMW PGA Championship this week after his tied-41st finish at the Amgen Irish Open on Sunday; watch all four rounds of the BMW PGA Championship live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
On Tuesday, the PGA Tour outlined new membership categories for its two-tier promotion-and-relegation structure , launching in 2028.

Two new series will run concurrently: the PGA Tour Championship Series and the PGA Tour Challenger Series

The Championship Series will feature the tour's top performers; players will move between both tiers depending on performance

The Championship Series will draw players from multiple categories, with the top 90 golfers retaining Championship Series membership; 20 players will be promoted from the Challenger Series

Two-year exemptions for the Championship Series will be granted for those who win a major championship or The Players

Under the current PGA Tour qualification structure, the top 10 players on the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai Rankings at the end of the season will win PGA Tour cards for the following season.

However, the PGA Tour did not confirm how many cards will be offered to top performers on the DP World Tour.

The PGA Tour said: "Access available to top performers from the DP World Tour is being considered as part of the ongoing discussions regarding the future of the Strategic Alliance."

Ahead of this week's BMW PGA Championship, McIlroy was asked if the new membership criteria was something to be worried about for DP World Tour players, he said: "No. I don't think so.

"I just think the conversation about the PGA Tour's structure has changed. From my point of view, I don't see any reason why a DP World Tour player would go to the Challenger Series.

"I don't see that as an upward move in your career. I see it as a very lateral move."

McIlroy finished tied-41st at last week's Amgen Irish Open, but ahead of the tournament, he predicted LIV Golf players would rejoin the DP World Tour and added the tour would only get stronger with their addition .

On Tuesday at Wentworth, McIlroy said he believed the PGA Tour's discussions with the DP World Tour centred on determining how many Championship Series cards it would be reasonable to award to the top players on the DP World Tour.

"I would imagine that's what the ongoing discussions are. From the DP World Tour, they're really trying to create something that is a viable alternative to the Challenger Series," he said.

"Obviously this is going to be a pathway to the Championship Series.

"No one is going to argue that the Championship Series is going to be the highest level of Tour golf that you can play, and then it's just deciding what an adequate number of cards is to go from the DP World Tour to the Championship Series.

"I don't see the Challenger Tour as a progression from the DP World Tour, and I would say a lot of players would feel similarly here."

McIlroy: I'd love to one day play solely on the DP World Tour

McIlroy has reduced his playing schedule over the past two years, after he finally ended his long wait to win The Masters in 2025.

Asked whether he would eventually one day consider playing the majority of his golf on the DP World Tour, McIlroy told Sky Sports News : "I'd love to envision a day where I am able to play solely on the DP World Tour.

"But in order to keep hold of your PGA Tour membership, you have to play a certain number of events.

"The fields are deep and you have to stay in that top 70 or 90 or whatever it is.

"One day, maybe. That would be really, really nice, to finish my career where I started my career.

"While I'm still in my prime, I'm just going to have to split my time as best as I can between both."

articles.title: Ryder Cup 2027: Team Europe stars give verdict on early trip to Adare Manor and 'fresh energy' for Luke Donald's side
articles.summary: Team Europe enjoyed a practice round at Adare Manor on Monday ahead of the Ryder Cup being hosted there next September; Several members of Luke Donald's side discussed the benefits of the team trip in their BMW PGA Championship press conferences
articles.body:
Although not quite a full scouting mission like Donald provided ahead of previous Ryder Cup wins at Marco Simone GC and Bethpage Black, it gave many of his potential players an early experience of tackling next year's Ryder Cup venue in Ireland.

A mix of established Ryder Cup members and likely rookie contenders made the trip after the Amgen Irish Open, with a team dinner followed by 18 holes on Monday

Sixteen players joined Donald and his vice-captains for the team session ahead of travelling onto the DP World Tour's BMW PGA Championship - 10 of last year's line-up, two more with past Ryder Cup pedigree and four potential debutants.

"Any time I'm asked to go to Adare Manor, I'm going to go happily and willingly," said Jon Rahm. "It's one of the best hotel golf course experiences there is in the world.

"It was a lot of fun. It was very enjoyable. I think those days are great for all of us to see each other and just in a way remember why we do what we do.

"For those players who have never been there before, I think it's just getting those first nerves out of the way of how they may feel.

Only Rory McIlroy and Rasmus Hojgaard were missing from Donald's dozen that celebrated a 15-13 victory in New York. Alex Noren - a winner in 2018 and vice-captain last year - and Nicolai Hojgaard, part of the 2023 team, also made the trip.

Alex Fitzpatrick and Kristoffer Reitan both featured after impressive rookie campaigns on the PGA Tour, while Spanish duo Eugenio Chacarra and Ángel Ayora were the other newcomers involved.

Most travelled straight from the Amgen Irish Open, with Shane Lowry a later arrival after his record-breaking 11-shot win on home soil at Trump International Golf Links.

"It was a lovely boys' day out, in the sense we got together and had a nice dinner," Justin Rose told the Sky Sports podcast . "There was some intention-setting of what it means to be on the team and what the plans are going forward.

"The round itself yesterday was very casual, very fun and just a first look at the golf course. Having Adare Manor pretty much to yourself is a pretty special experience.

"For them [rookies], it lights the fire even more in them to want to be a part of that team. It gives them the comfort to feel like they're already part of the team, in the sense of [being in] Luke's thoughts, the way of doing things and how the captain goes about it.

"It doesn't necessarily feel like a game-changing trip and 'wow, we have an advantage' or anything like that, but I think it's very important in terms of culture setting and all that."

The European players went out in groups of four for a round in calm conditions, with some playing the course for the first time and others refamiliarizing themselves with a venue that previously hosted the JP McManus Pro-Am.

"With the good weather they've had in Europe, in Ireland, it was in as good a shape as I've ever seen it," Rahm added. "It was actually firm. They could have had it as fast as they wanted to.

"It wasn't overly fast because obviously I think they want the public to still enjoy the week. It was in perfect condition. It was immaculate."

The last two Ryder Cups in Europe have been on venues used for regular DP World Tour events, with Le Golf National (2018) a past site of the Open de France and Marco Simone GC (2023) the Open d'Italia, giving Donald a different challenge in Ireland.

"The strategy around setting up the course is very different from when they have a lot of data from the [DP World] Tour," Noren explained. "It's a very difficult task to set that up, I think, to our advantage. We'll see how they do.

"It's the course and the resources where you can set it up pretty much however you want - you can grow in the rough, you can expand, and you can use tee boxes. It's like not particularly a blank sheet of paper, but you can do whatever you want."

Who else was missing and what happens next?

PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai was invited but unable to attend due to a close friend's wedding in Portugal on Sunday, while Tom McKibbin - who played two rounds with Donald in Ireland last week - was not involved.

Ryder Cup qualification is already under way, with points only available via the Race to Dubai standings for the rest of this season before including FedExCup points in January, with Rose expecting to see some new editions in Team Europe next September.

"I think freshening it up a little bit would be a good thing," Rose admitted. "You want your team to be experienced but to have some fresh energy is always great. Whether that be ideas, style of game, pairing options - to change is up is a good thing.

"There's plenty of opportunity for guys to break through. I think the transition from Whistling Straits (2021) into Rome was fantastic and I think that only strengthened into solidifying some of those players that stepped into that role at Bethpage.

There are so many good young players, like the Højgaards [Nicolai and Rasmus], Ludvig [Åberg], even Bob [MacIntyre]. Those guys are now real stalwarts of the team. There has been a great transition in Europe, so we can afford another new batch of youngsters."

Could consistency be key again for Team Europe?

Europe carried 11 of their 12-man line-up and four of the five vice-captains from their 2023 victory to New York in 2025, with the Molinari brothers - Edoardo and Francesco - already confirmed for a third consecutive stint in Donald's backroom team.

Padraig Harrington has been added as a vice-captain on home soil, while McIlroy anticipates the bulk of Donald's last two teams to be back together again in Ireland.

"If there's ever a place to blend rookies, it is in Europe," McIlroy told Sky Sports . "The thing that I preach around the European Ryder Cup team is there's this continuity.

"I think continuity between the captain, the players, the vice captains is a big thing in a team environment. Look, inevitably there might be some new faces on that team, but I don't think there's certainly not going to be wholesale changes.

"I think the nucleus of our team will remain the nucleus. You might have a couple [new] maybe, but I'd say for the most part, as long as everyone plays well and stays injury-free, you're going to have a very similar looking team to what we've had the last couple."

The Ryder Cup will be held from September 17-19 next year, live on Sky Sports . Donald will be looking to be the first captain in history to win three consecutive Ryder Cups.

articles.title: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings confirms plan to stage Play-Offs in Middle East, despite player safety concerns
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings discussed the plans for the season-ending Play-Offs, the Strategic Alliance with the PGA Tour and the bright future the tour has within the global game
articles.body:
The Abu Dhabi Championship is scheduled to be held at Yas Links on November 5-8, before the Race to Dubai season reaches its climax at the DP World Tour Championship the following week.

There has been speculation throughout the season over whether both events would move to a different country, with Formula 1 cancelling two events earlier in the year in the region and discussions ongoing over whether races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead.

Matt Fitzpatrick and Bob MacIntyre were among players to express concerns about travelling to the UAE, despite a relaxing of the previous "all but essential travel" guidelines from the UK's Foreign Office, with Kinnings hopeful both events can take place as planned.

"A lot of people are asking and it's an obvious question," Kinnings told Sky Sports . "The reality is we expect every intention to be playing in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

"Work has started and we're building stuff at Yas Links and at the Jumeirah Golf Estates, so our intention is to go ahead.

"We clearly need to keep in touch with travel advisors and other people who help with us, but our plan is definitely to play the Play-Offs in the UAE."

Defending DP World Tour champion Fitzpatrick said on Wednesday that he was "not that comfortable" playing in Dubai, given its proximity to the conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel, although McIlroy was less concerned.

"If the local governments feel like it's safe to put on these events, they are not going to put their citizens or people visiting in harm's way," McIlroy said after his opening round at the BMW PGA Championship.

"I love the Middle East. I have a lot of friends there and I'm looking forward to going back for sure."

The DP World Tour announced its 2027 schedule at the BMW PGA Championship, with the Flagship Event being held a week later next year and immediately after the centenary Ryder Cup at Adare Manor.

JJ Spaun and Ryan Gerard were among the limited American players to make the trip over to England for the event, despite more spots being available to PGA Tour players, although Kinnings hopes to see more make the journey in the future.

" I think the future schedule will lend itself to that," Kinnings said. "We've got a great working relationship with the PGA Tour and we're working with them on what the future will look like.

"I think the way the schedule's set up, with golf in America stopping at the end of August, we've got the opportunity to shine from September 1 until the end of January. I think that'll mean more of the guys will come and play in great events like this and some of the other tournaments as well."

Kinnings added: "I have to say, I couldn't be more excited. I think it's a huge opportunity for international golf. We clearly have wonderful players and we have an opportunity to shine in the schedule."

The DP World Tour has yet to announce whether it will impose sanctions for its members wishing to play in the new iteration of the LIV Golf League, should LIV 2.0 go ahead as planned in 2027, with Kinnings keen to see the strongest fields possible on his circuit.

"We've been very consistent on the whole question and we're going to continue that way," Kinnings insisted. "What will happen with LIV is entirely speculation, but from our perspective we want to find a balance. As a business, we just love to have the best fields we possibly can with the best players.

"But we're also a member's organisation and our job is purely to make sure we look out for the best interests of the members. We have a wonderful tour, amazing culture and that's because of the players, so nothing's going to change on that front.

"I think we're in a stronger position as we can possibly be. We've got great partners and the future looks bright - we now just need to work out exactly what it looks like."

articles.title: Rory McIlroy switches focus to battle with Patrick Reed for Race to Dubai title after near-miss at BMW PGA Championship
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy moved within 307.76 points of Patrick Reed in the Race to Dubai rankings with a tied-second finish at the BMW PGA Championship; McIlroy is looking to win the Order of Merit for an eighth time; JJ Spaun claimed a two-shot win at Wentworth
articles.body:
McIlroy went into the final round two strokes back at Wentworth, where he recovered from failing to convert numerous birdie chances to briefly grab a share of the lead during a thrilling final round.

The world No 2 stumbled to a closing par to post a final-round 68 and finish in tied-second on 15 under, two strokes behind winner JJ Spaun, leaving McIlroy with a fourth runner-up finish at the DP World Tour's flagship event since his 2014 win.

"I had my chances out there!" McIlroy told Sky Sports . "I felt like I hit the ball really well - probably the best I've hit it all week.

"Had good chances on two, three, five, eight, nine, 10, 13, the last. I felt like I hit good putts but, a bit like last week [Amgen Irish Open], I was just not seeing the lines that well.

"I struggled with some of the reads today and I hit some good putts that didn't go in. I holed a couple coming down the stretch but I think the story of the week was that I didn't hole as much as I should have.

"If I did, it would have been a different story."

Will Reed stop McIlroy's Race to Dubai title bid?

McIlroy ending in a four-way share of second earned him 532 Race to Dubai points and moved him within 308 of Reed, who withdrew mid-round on Friday due to injury, in the season-long standings.

Reed had said he was looking forward to a battle with McIlroy, who will next feature at the DP World India Championship from October 15-18 before the two season-ending DP World Tour Play-Offs in the Middle East.

The Northern Irishman has topped the Order of Merit in four consecutive seasons and is looking to finish No 1 again, which would pull McIlroy level with Colin Montgomerie's all-time tally of eight Race to Dubai titles.

"As soon as The Open was over, really that was the goal for the rest of the year," McIlroy added. "I would obviously love to do it [win the Race to Dubai].

"For Patrick, it was unfortunate this week. Hopefully he's okay and he can play what he needs to going in to really make it a good battle, but I'm excited.

"I'll keep working on my game over the next three weeks, then hopefully have a strong end to the season and give myself a great chance at that eighth one."

McIlroy's runner-up finish at Wentworth follows previous seconds there in 2018, 2022 and 2024, leaving him still searching for his first worldwide win since successfully defending his Masters title in April.

"I think McIlroy left a little bit behind him on the greens - he had loads of chances," former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports .

"It was surprising for a guy who has really improved his putting over the past couple of years and looks so good over them, but he seemed to miss putt after putt after putt.

"I don't think he has played his best golf from tee to green, I'd rate him 3.5 out of five for what he's capable of. It's almost like he couldn't get out of the starting blocks but still finishes tied-second - it's incredible and shows just how much talent he has."

McIlroy is next scheduled to feature at the DP World India Championship from October 15-18, before further appearances at the Abu Dhabi Championship (November 5-8) and the DP World Tour Championship (November 12-15).

articles.title: BMW PGA Championship: How JJ Spaun used Team USA snub for Presidents Cup as motivation for dramatic Wentworth victory
articles.summary: JJ Spaun claimed a two-shot win at the BMW PGA Championship; Spaun discussed missing out on Team USA's Presidents Cup side and why him and his wife are obsessed with Jeremy Clarkson after his debut victory at Wentworth
articles.body:
Spaun became the first player since Byeong Hun An in 2015 to win the DP World Tour's flagship event on debut, posting a final-round 67 to claim a two-shot success over Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai, Adam Scott and Manuel Elvira.

Last year's US Open champion also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open and finished 10th in the Presidents Cup qualification standings, having also made his Team USA debut in the Ryder Cup last September.

Spaun was controversially overlooked for a captain's pick by Brandt Snedeker in his line-up to face the International Team in the biennial contest, live from Thursday on Sky Sports , with the 36-year-old pleased to respond by claiming a statement victory.

"The stars aligned this week for me to come out on top," Spaun said. "I'm just grateful to have the opportunity and play well and give myself a chance and came out with a W.

"We [him and Snedeker] haven't spoken. I played with a huge chip on my shoulder. I definitely had something to prove this week, but everything happens for a reason. I'm so delighted to be here and just to even play this event.

"The extra motivation, I think that is the willpower that you have. Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple weeks ago was very disappointing and I wanted to prove that I deserve to be on that team.

"I took care of my business this week, so all the best to the team next week at Medinah - I'll be watching from my couch!"

Spaun said he had good conversations with Snedeker during the qualification campaign and believed he would feature at Medinah, but was handed the unwanted news in a short phone call after the season-ending Tour Championship.

"It was like a 45-second phone call," Spaun revealed in his press conference. "Just said I wasn't on the team and said I was the odd man out. I wished him luck and that was it.

"It [past conversations] led me to believe that I would make the team."

Spaun added: "I was pretty determined this week to kind of prove something. My whole career, I've kind of had to do that. I wasn't given scholarships. I had to earn my PGA Tour card the hard way. I was never given sponsor invite opportunities - I just had to do everything the hard way.

"Being left off was obviously for a reason. I don't know what that reason was, but I'm here now and there was a reason why we're here. My caddie kept telling me that and it's crazy how this has happened."

Why did Spaun celebrate win with a Jeremy Clarkson mask?

Spaun celebrated victory with his wife, Melody, who brought a mask of broadcaster Jeremy Clarkson around the course during various points of the week.

"We've grown fond of him [Jeremy Clarkson], along with the English culture," Spaun explained. "We actually take holidays in December in the Cotswolds and we really enjoy his show [Clarkson's Farm]. I went to his pub The Farmer's Dog, with the hopes to catch a glimpse of him, but he wasn't around.

"Yeah, she [his wife Melody] said we would have a surprise guest following this week if I competed in the tournament and sure enough it was Thursday morning - I see the face of Jeremy Clarkson and her holding it.

"Jeremy was there in spirit and I think he brought me good fortune!"

articles.title: PGA Tour: Jacob Bridgeman races to Biltmore Championship victory to provide Team USA form boost for Presidents Cup
articles.summary: Jacob Bridgeman won the Genesis Invitational in February and is now a multiple PGA Tour winner; Bridgeman will represent Team USA for the first time at the Presidents Cup, live on Thursday from 5pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Bridgeman, named among Brandt Snedeker's captain's picks for Team USA to face the International Team at Medinah, overturned a five-shot deficit during a low-scoring final day in Asheville, North Carolina.

The world No 29 raced through the field by carding an eagle and eight birdies during a bogey-free 61 at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove, lifting him to 26 under and two shots clear of compatriot Ben James, who matched his 61.

Bridgeman, 26, birdied three of his opening four holes and holed from 10 feet to eagle the par-five eighth, before picking up a shot at the 10th and posting three more in a row from the 13th.

He needed to play his last three holes in three under to card his first sub-60 round on the PGA Tour, but a birdie at the par-five 17th and closing par was enough for a second PGA Tour win of the year.

"It's a dream come true," Bridgeman said about representing Team USA, live from Thursday on Sky Sports . "There is so much individualness in this sport, but to be able to play as a team and the United States is just amazing.

"Everybody is pumped. It's getting really real. We're all getting super excited!"

Overnight leader Neal Shipley finished three strokes back in tied-third alongside Ricky Castillo, with fellow American JT Poston narrowly missing out on a '59 round' as he jumped into a share of fifth alongside Jackson Koivun, who will also feature in the Presidents Cup.

"At the end of the day it was a great round of golf, a new career low out here," Poston said, having two-putted from 25 feet to par his final hole as he carded a 60. "As much as I would like to shoot that magical 59 number, which I've never done, there are so many positives to take away."

Ireland's Seamus Power ended six strokes back in a share of seventh, with England's Marco Penge - a notable absentee from the DP World Tour's BMW PGA Championship - finishing in a share of 10th after a final-round 67.

articles.title: Sandy Scott earns promotion to PGA Tour after Ohio victory
articles.summary: Scotland's Sandy Scott puts a career-threatening wrist injury behind him to earn promotion to the main PGA Tour for the first time after winning the Nationwide Children's Hospital Championship in Columbus, Ohio.
articles.body:
Scotland's Sandy Scott has put a career-threatening wrist injury behind him to earn promotion to the main PGA Tour for the first time by winning the Nationwide Children's Hospital Championship in Columbus, Ohio.

The 28-year-old's one-stroke victory on Sunday was his first on the Korn Ferry Tour and lifted him to second spot on the development tour's points list.

It came a week after he finished runner-up at the Simmons Bank Open for the Snedeker Foundation in Franklin, Tennessee.

The Nairn golfer needed two surgeries after tearing ligaments in his right wrist in 2019 and admitted: "I was in some really low times and didn't know if I'd ever play golf again."

MacIntyre finishes equal 10th as Spaun wins PGA Championship

Scott battled back from that but withdrew from this season's BMW Charity Pro-Am and missed two months of the season after the wrist flared up again.

"It was just getting progressively worse," he told the Golf Channel. "Every day, it was harder to warm up and I was getting a bit more sharp pain.

"With having a history of having a wrist injury, I've kind of gone through the waves of being unsure about what golf's going to look like for me in the future.

"When I did come back from it in college, I had this overwhelming sense of perspective that I'm just happy to be out here competing, fulfilling this dream that I've always had of playing golf professionally. To be able to play well has been a bonus."

Scott started his latest event in 13th place on the tour, but he birdied two of his final three holes to close with a six-under 65 on the Scarlet Course at Ohio State University Golf Club to post 18-under 266 and break the 72-hole tournament record, edging out American John Marshall Butler for the win.

He becomes the seventh player - and first European - to have qualified for the main tour during the 2027 season.

Scott had finished 55th in his rookie season on the development tour last year but will next year return to a PGA Tour event for the first time since the 2020 US Open at Winged Foot Golf Club, when he qualified by finishing sixth in the World Amateur Golf Ranking.

"It's been a weird journey and I'm just so happy," he said.

articles.title: Southern Miss QB Ethan Hampton likely out vs Tulane, coach Blake Anderson says
articles.summary: Southern Miss football coach Blake Anderson said starting quarterback Ethan Hampton is unlikely to play vs Tulane because of a hand injury
articles.body:
Southern Miss football starting quarterback Ethan Hampton is unlikely to play in Week 4 against Tulane .

Golden Eagles' coach Blake Anderson provided an update on Hampton's injury status on Sept. 21, two days after the quarterback injured his throwing hand against UConn . Anderson called Hampton's hand injury "pretty significant" and said he does not expect him to play against the Green Wave on Sept. 26.

"He's beat up," Anderson said. "We do not anticipate him being able to squeeze and throw a football this week."

Hampton did not play in the second half of Southern Miss ' 48-20 loss to the Huskies. During the first half, Hampton hit his throwing hand on another player's helmet and was unable to hold a football at halftime. After the game, Anderson said that Hampton did not break any bones.

The senior quarterback injured the same hand on Aug. 15, suffering a bone bruise during the Golden Eagles ' first scrimmage of the preseason. Hampton missed two weeks of practice as he recovered from the injury.

Southern Miss QB Ethan Hampton likely out vs Tulane, coach Blake Anderson says

Anderson is unsure about what Hampton's recovery timeline will look like this time.

"Don't know how long this thing will last," Anderson said. "It's a little different than last (time). It's in the same area, but not the exact same. We're still getting some more images back to find out exactly what all is wrong, but he's clearly not in a position to play."

Hampton has 419 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and four interceptions this season.

Southern Miss (1-2) will play Tulane (1-2) at Yulman Stadium on Sept. 26 (6 p.m. CT, ESPN+).

Who will play QB for Southern Miss vs Tulane?

Senior quarterback Landry Lyddy replaced Hampton in the second half against UConn. He completed 14 of 25 passes for 194 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

"Lyddy came in and did a pretty good job in his absence," Anderson said. "I have no doubt he'll do everything he can to be prepared."

Lyddy competed with Hampton for the starting quarterback job throughout the preseason. He also served as the Golden Eagles' backup in 2025, playing in six games and starting against Texas State on Nov. 11.

In his lone start last year, he completed 29 of 44 passes for 267 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Southern Miss lost the game 41-14.

Sophomore quarterback John White will move from third-string to backup quarterback, and freshman Hugh Price will be the team's new third-string.

articles.title: Kyler Murray injury update: Vikings QB cleared to start in Week 3
articles.summary: The Vikings are set to welcome Kyler Murray back to the lineup for NFL Week 3 after the QB suffered a concussion in the season opener.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings ' long sought sense of quarterback normalcy might not be far off.

Starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been cleared from the concussion protocol and is set to start the Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , coach Kevin O'Connell announced on Monday, Sept. 21.

Murray was knocked out of the season-opening win against the Green Bay Packers on the third series of the game. After scrambling to his right, the signal-caller took a big hit from Packers safety Javon Bullard and edge rusher Lukas Van Ness .

He was replaced in the game by backup Carson Wentz , who went on to start the Week 2 victory over the Chicago Bears .

In Sunday's rain-soaked divisional matchup, however, Minnesota was held without a touchdown. Wentz completed 11 of 20 passes for just 143 yards.

Murray, who signed a one-year, $1.3 million contract with the Vikings this offseason after being released by the Arizona Cardinals in March, was named Minnesota's starting quarterback in August following a brief competition with incumbent first-stringer J.J. McCarthy . Wentz was installed as the backup while McCarthy was relegated to an emergency role .

articles.title: Presidents Cup 2026: Teams, captains, venue, format and how players qualified for Team USA vs Internationals at Medinah
articles.summary: Team USA chase a record-extending 11th consecutive Presidents Cup victory over the International Team; Brandt Snedeker captains the United States at Medinah and Geoff Ogilvy leads the Internationals; watch live coverage this week on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The Presidents Cup is a biennial team competition run by the PGA Tour that sees the United States take on the International Team, which covers the rest of the world outside of Europe.

The event has been played since 1994 and alternates between being held in the United States and elsewhere, with Canada, South Korea, Australia and South Africa all past host nations.

The Presidents Cup is back to even-numbered years to avoid clashing with the Ryder Cup, which moved to odd-numbered years after being postponed in 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

This year's edition takes place from September 24-27 at Medinah Country Club in Illinois, which hosted the 2012 Ryder Cup along with the US Open and PGA Championship on multiple occasions.

The 2028 edition will be held at Kingston Heath Golf Club in Victoria, Australia, while the 2030 contest goes to Bellerive Country Club in Missouri.

Team USA's qualification period began in January 2025 and ran until the BMW Championship last month, with points earned based on PGA Tour results and the top six in the standings qualifying automatically.

Every FedExCup point was worth one qualification point for all events in 2025 and 1.5 points last season, with FedExCup points earned at The Players or in majors in 2026 worth two points.

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler topped the standings after winning eight times during the qualification period, with Players champion Cameron Young and US Open winner Wyndham Clark the next in the standings ahead of Sam Burns, Russell Henley and Collin Morikawa.

Captain Brandt Snedeker then selected Jacob Bridgeman, Patrick Cantlay, Chris Gotterup, Jackson Koivun, Xander Schauffele and Justin Thomas as his six picks.

The International Team standings ran from September 8 until the Tour Championship on August 30, with players' Official World Golf Ranking Points being used to determine their six automatic spots.

Si Woo Kim topped the standings to secure his fourth appearance and Ryan Fox earned a debut by winning The Open at Royal Birkdale, with Hideki Matsuyama, Min Woo Lee, Tom Kim and Adam Scott all returning to the International Team.

Sungjae Im, Nico Echavarria, Corey Conners, Nick Taylor, Christiaan Bezuidenhout and Ryo Hisatsune were Geoff Ogilvy's six captain's picks, with seven different nationalities making up the International Team.

Snedeker served as a vice-captain at the 2024 Presidents Cup and 2025 Ryder Cup before taking on the American captaincy, with the 45-year-old having Gary Woodland, Jim Furyk, Keegan Bradley and Webb Simpson as his assistants.

Ogilvy appeared in three consecutive Presidents Cups as a player from 2007 and now takes on the captaincy for the first time, succeeding Mike Weir. The Australian has Trevor Immelman, Tim Clark, Taylor Pendrith and Camilo Villegas as his four assistants.

Who are favourites and what happened last time?

Team USA secured a record-extending 10th consecutive Presidents Cup victory with an 18.5-11.5 success over the International Team in the 2024 edition.

The Americans won 7.5 of the 12 points on offer in the Sunday singles to continue their dominance, which has seen them win 13 of the previous Presidents Cups.

A tie in the 2003 edition and a lone victory in 1998 are the only occasions to date where the International Team has avoided defeat, with the visitors coming in as underdogs once again.

What is the format and how similar is it to the Ryder Cup?

Players compete in sessions of fourballs, foursomes and singles - just like Team USA does when they face Europe in the Ryder Cup - although the Presidents Cup has more matches in the opening two sessions and spreads the contest out across four days.

Thursday's play is fourballs and sees two golfers from each team compete but each player uses their own ball, with the lowest score from each pair counting towards their total in that match.

Friday's action is foursomes , containing five matches of two golfers from the United States competing against a pair from the International Team. Team members alternate between shots and each team uses one ball.

A double session sees fourballs and fourballs played on Saturday, before all players compete in the Sunday singles and every member from the USA team plays against an International opponent in a head-to-head contest.

A total of 30 points are available across the four days, with the team with the most points then claiming the trophy. Team USA need 15 points - as defending champions - to retain, while either team would need 15.5 points for victory.

The Presidents Cup is run by the PGA Tour, which continues to ban LIV Golf players from competing in its events since the breakaway circuit was launched in 2022.

Joaquin Niemann of Chile finished third in the LIV Golf season-long standings and was part of the 2019 competition before leaving the PGA Tour, while Australia's Lucas Herbert was another to have an impressive season on the circuit.

Former Open champions Cameron Smith and Louis Oosthuizen are others who have previously represented the International Team but no longer can, while Bryson DeChambeau is among those unable to represent Team USA.

When does play start and what time does coverage begin on Sky Sports?

Sky Sports will have live coverage from every session, with coverage getting under way at 5.30pm for Thursday's fourballs ahead of the first tee shot at 5.35pm (11.35am local time).

Friday's foursomes action starts at 7pm before the first match begins at 7.05pm (1.05pm local time), while Saturday's fourballs coverage begins at 1pm on Sky Sports+ and 5.30pm on Sky Sports Golf.

The afternoon foursomes are then live on Saturday from 7pm, with full coverage of the Sunday singles starting at 5pm on Sky Sports Golf and running until long after a winner has been crowned.

The Presidents Cup is one of three events live on Sky Sports this week, with the DP World Tour's Open de France and the LPGA Tour's Walmart Nw Arkansas Championship - its first event since the Solheim Cup - also available to enjoy.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy vs Nelly Korda? Could a Ryder Cup-Solheim Cup style mixed team event ever happen and how would it work?
articles.summary: Team Europe captain Luke Donald recently suggested the idea of a mixed team event, similar to the Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup, but could it work and what challenges would it face? watch the Presidents Cup live this week on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup both see the best from Europe take on the United States, while the Presidents Cup - live this week on Sky Sports - is a biennial contest between Team USA and an International Team.

The Grant Thornton Invitational is a mixed team tournament taking place every December containing PGA Tour and DP World Tour players, following on from the defunct JCPenney Classic, but is there space for one on an international scale?

A mixed team golf event will feature in the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, while Team Europe captain Luke Donald recently suggested launching a mixed team event that would share similarities with the Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup.

"I'm all for having some events where we're playing together and sharing each other's talents," Donald told the Telegraph ahead of the BMW PGA Championship. "I think it's great to see that.

"Who wouldn't want to see a Nelly Korda or Charley Hull playing with a Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm or Scottie Scheffler - some of the best in the world in the men's and women's games?"

Donald did caveat that the creation of a mixed Europe vs America team event would "take some time to create", plus added it would be difficult to find a time in the calendar for the event.

"It's great in principle but, when you get down to the practicalities of it, where it's going to fit in the calendar?" Ryder Cup-winning captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports.

"Are the players going to play another team event, particularly when they're probably not going to get paid for it? They're the complexities of it, but it's great in theory.

The Ryder Cup, Solheim Cup and Presidents Cup all traditionally take place in September, following the end of the PGA Tour season, with the DP World Tour schedule the main focus in men's golf during the autumn.

Sky Sports Golf podcast - subscribe now on: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | Spreaker

"The more team stuff and the more golf we have, I think is great, but the schedule is getting tighter and tighter," former DP World Tour player Anthony Wall told the Sky Sports Golf podcast .

"You've got golf in the Olympics and it's getting harder and harder for guys to commit - that is the issue. We've tried a number of different things over the years and it's just about weeks, it really is so difficult."

Could the Presidents Cup be boosted by being mixed?

The idea of a mixed Presidents Cup has previously been debated to make the contest more balanced, with Team USA heading to Medinah this week chasing a record-extending 11th consecutive win over the International Team.

Five of the world's top six in the women's game - as of September 22 - would be eligible to represent an International side based on the current Presidents Cup format, where the United States face the rest of the world except Europe.

"Maybe they [the PGA Tour] go into a partnership with the LPGA Tour to create something like that," McGinley added. "Whether they do it for the Presidents Cup is doubtful, because they've already said no to that situation evolving.

"They may open up a new pathway for it, you never know, but it does make a lot of sense to do that because then you would get two really good, balanced teams.

"If you add half of the ladies internationally combined with the men, you would have a pretty formidable team and a team that would be very strong against the might of America."

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: Jordan Love can cook, but his teammates need to allow him to do so
articles.summary: When Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was arrested earlier this year, many fans assumed he would be suspended by the NFL. Currently on the commissi...
articles.body:
When Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was arrested earlier this year, many fans assumed he would be suspended by the NFL. Currently on the commissioner's exempt list after pleading no contest to charges related to domestic violence, Jacobs has yet to play for the Packers this season. Obviously, this is what many expected.

To that end, fans were excited for the notion that star quarterback Jordan Love would be allowed to "cook." That is, head coach Matt LaFleu r would give Love more control of the offense by letting him call more plays on his own and/or throw the ball more.

In theory, it is a fantastic idea. In practice (games), it has been a struggle.

The rest of the Green Bay Packers offense needs to elevate themselves to let Jordan Love lead them

In order for Love, or any quarterback for that matter, to be successful, he needs his offensive line to protect him and his wide receivers to catch the passes that he throws to them. Over the course of the first two games, this has not happened on a consistent basis.

At 1-1, Green Bay has the entire season ahead of them. However, injuries and poor play on the offensive side of the ball have fans concerned that the year could slip away from them.

In Week One, for instance, the Packers offensive line allowed the Minnesota Vikings to pressure Love 22 times. While they improved in Week Two against the New York Jets , allowing just six pressures, Love's average 2.41-2.45 seconds time to throw is the lowest (worst) in the league.

If Love is given even just a little extra time to throw, it will allow plays to develop down field, pass catchers to get open, and the quarterback himself to be in a better physical position to throw.

At the same time, his pass catchers need to, well, catch. Through the first two games of the 2026 NFL season, Green Bay has dropped seven passes.

These mental and technique errors can be fixed. Putting a healthy offensive line in front of Love would also be beneficial. Unfortunately, that has proven to be a challenge through the first two weeks of the season, and it is not exactly clear what the Packers' plan is going forward has injuries continue to stack up.

All this to say that Love is more than capable of being an MVP-caliber quarterback. However, even the best QB's in the league will not be very productive if they do not have time to throw and/or their receivers do not catch passes that hit them in the hands.

Everyone, including Packers players, want to see Love cook in 2026. His teammates need to allow him to do so.

articles.title: Presidents Cup 2026 Rules, Format and Points System Primer for Golf Tournament
articles.summary: The United States will attempt to extend their dominance in the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.
articles.body:
The United States will attempt to extend their dominance in the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.

Team USA won all but two of the bi-annual showdowns with the International Team since the Presidents Cup debuted in 1994.

Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young and Wyndham Clark headline the American team that is a heavy favorite to win on home soil.

The International team is made up of the best golfers from Canada, Mexico, South America, Africa and Asia. No Europeans are eligible because they participate in the Ryder Cup.

A total of 30 points are up for grabs from Thursday to Sunday. Team USA's scored at least 16 points in each of the last four Presidents Cups.

The Presidents Cup takes place over four days.

Thursday's five matches will be in the four-balls format where every golfer plays every stroke. The lowest score in the partnership on each hole is counted for the score.

Friday's five matches are contested in the foursomes, which is an alternate shot format.

On Saturday, four four-balls and a quarter of foursomes matches will be played across the morning and afternoon sessions.

Sunday's play features 12 singles matches.

The team with the most points on Sunday comes away with the Presidents Cup.

The winner of each match receives one point. If a match is tied after 18 holes, the two teams receive a half point.

Team USA: Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Sam Burns, Russell Henley, Collin Morikawa, Chris Gotterup, Xander Schauffele, Justin Thomas, Jacob Bridgeman, Patrick Cantlay, Jackson Koivun

International: Si-Woo Kim, Ryan Fox, Hideki Matsuayama, Min Woo Lee, Tom Kim, Adam Scott, Corey Conners, Nico Echevarria, Sung-Jae Im, Ryo Hisatsune, Nick Taylor, Christian Bezuidenhout

Scheffler, Young and Clark are the most notable names on the Team USA roster. They have plenty of match-play experience around them in the form of Justin Thomas, Collin Morikawa and Xander Schauffele.

Chris Gotterup, Jacob Bridgeman and Jackson Koivun are the rookies on the American roster. Schauffele, Thomas and Patrick Cantlay are all making their third Presidents Cup appearances.

Four Presidents Cup rookies are on the International roster, including The Open champion Ryan Fox.

Seven players on the International roster have appeared in multiple Presidents Cups, but none of them have come away as winners.

Team USA is viewed as the clear favorite given its star-studded roster and history in the event.

An International win would go down as one of the more shocking results in the event's history.
