articles.summary: it's the first day of practice at the Presidents Cup, the golf tournament happening at the famed Medinah County Club Golf Course.
articles.body:
It's the first day of practice at the Presidents Cup, the golf tournament happening at the famed Medinah County Club Golf Course.

It's been years in the making, and now is just days away from the start of The President's Cup here at Medinah Country Club. And what a week it's going be.

Medinah is rolling out the red carpet for some the best golfers in the world. The President's Cup is a bi-annual event pitting the U.S. Team against a team made up of the best international players outside of Europe.

Medinah is no stranger to major golf events.

President Trump is visiting Chicago sometime in the coming days for the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club.

Mike Gilligan with the Chicago District for Golf Association talks about the Presidents Cup.

Mike Gilligan from the Chicago District Golf Association said hosting the President's Cup puts Medinah in a very special place in golf history.

"This place just never disappoints," Gilligan said. "It is one of the greatest arenas to host a major exhibition, championship or otherwise. I think its location means everything. It is so easy to get to form the North Shore, from the south suburbs and the western suburbs. I just think it is the ultimate venue in golf here in Chicago."

It takes more than a village to pull off a massive event like this. Volunteers come from around the area to serve as marshals around the course and work the merchandise tent.

"We have two types of marshals," Paul Grane said. "We have roving marshals and we have hole marshals. The roving marshal committee is a group of 46 people that volunteered to basically act as fore caddies during the tournament. There are four people per match. As balls go left or right, our team are the people that actually go to the balls, help with spectator management, help them get out of the way so the match can carry on and then we stay ahead of the match every time.

Besides being a great event for fans, The President's Cup generates millions of dollars for charity. Several local organizations like the Chicago District Golf Association and the First Tee have already received generous donations.

The Tournament starts on Thursday morning and ends on Sunday.

articles.title: Falcons vs. Packers bold predictions for Thursday Night Football clash in Week 3
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons (0-2) head to Lambeau Field to face the Green Bay Packers (1-1) in a Week 3 Thursday Night Football showdown that carries far more weight...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons (0-2) head to Lambeau Field to face the Green Bay Packers (1-1) in a Week 3 Thursday Night Football showdown that carries far more weight than a typical September game. Green Bay enters as roughly a 7-point home favorite with the total set around 44.5, and Atlanta arrives desperate to avoid an 0-3 hole with Michael Penix Jr. cleared to start after being listed with a knee injury. It's the Packers' long-awaited home opener, and both rosters are dealing with notable absences, from Jawaan Taylor and A.J. Terrell nursing injuries for Atlanta to Green Bay's own banged-up unit. Here are three bold predictions for this early-season measuring stick.

Michael Penix Jr. Silences the Doubters With a Multi-Touchdown Night

Michael Penix's return under center is the single biggest storyline heading into Thursday, and the bold call here is that he doesn't just play, he thrives. After being ruled out and then cleared through the week, Penix gets a green light against a Packers defense that has shown vulnerabilities against mobile, quick-releasing quarterbacks early in the season.

Expect Atlanta's coaching staff to lean on quick-hitting concepts and play-action to protect their banged-up offensive line, particularly with Taylor questionable at right tackle. Penix throws for at least two touchdowns and pushes 250-plus passing yards, connecting early and often with Drake London to keep the Falcons competitive against the spread even if Green Bay controls the scoreboard late. The bigger surprise wouldn't be Penix struggling in his return, it would be him outplaying Jordan Love 's overall efficiency for large stretches of the game.

Green Bay's Ground Game Disappoints, Forcing Love Into a 35-Pass Attempt Night

Green Bay's home opener hype will center on a run-heavy identity, but the bold prediction is that the Packers can't establish anything consistent on the ground against Atlanta's front seven. That shifts the burden squarely onto Jordan Love , who ends up throwing the ball more than 35 times as Green Bay searches for answers.

With the Falcons' secondary already thin at cornerback due to Terrell's groin issue, Love finds success spreading the ball to his receiving corps, and one pass-catcher in particular becomes the story of the night by clearing 90 receiving yards. The offensive imbalance doesn't cost Green Bay the win, but it makes the game far closer through three quarters than the near touchdown spread would suggest, and it sets up a nervy finish at Lambeau.

Under 44.5 Cashes as Both Defenses Bend but Don't Break

Despite the offensive talent on both sides, the bold prediction for the scoreboard is that this game stays under the posted total of 44.5, with defense and turnovers defining the outcome more than explosive plays. Atlanta's defense, even without full strength up front, gets at least one takeaway off Love in the red zone that swings field position, while Green Bay's defense forces a similar mistake from Penix in his first real test back from injury.

Both teams settle for field goals on multiple scoring drives rather than converting touchdowns in the red zone, a common theme for divisional and cross-conference games this early in the season when timing and chemistry are still developing. Green Bay wins a game that finishes closer to 24-17 than a blowout, covering the spread comfortably while the under hits, rewarding bettors who trust that this Thursday night clash will be decided by execution in the trenches rather than a shootout through the air.
